subject.title: Remote skill bin probe times out when node is co-located with gateway (macOS app as node on same host)

question: Should OpenClaw treat macOS app-backed nodes as immediately eligible for automatic remote skill bin probing, or should the gateway defer/skip/back off probes for app/co-located nodes until explicit readiness is proven?
rationale: The current code supports macOS app `system.which` and `system.run`, so the remaining fix is a policy choice across startup latency, remote skill discoverability, co-located app behavior, and documented node exec behavior.

options.title: Defer and back off app-node probes
options.body: Keep remote macOS skill support but delay initial probes and add bounded backoff/readiness checks for app-backed nodes.

options.title: Skip co-located app nodes
options.body: Avoid probing app nodes on the gateway host while continuing to probe true remote macOS nodes that advertise shell commands.

options.title: Keep current immediate probing
options.body: Accept startup/reconnect warnings as the cost of making remote skill bin availability visible as soon as a node connects.

recommendation.title: Defer and back off app-node probes
recommendation.body: Keep remote macOS skill support but delay initial probes and add bounded backoff/readiness checks for app-backed nodes.

likelyOwner.reason: He appears to have introduced the mac node exec policy and remote skills hot reload behavior that owns the core policy tradeoff.
